Unit 7, Passage 1.
The Secrets to Designing a Good Website Designing a good website requires careful planning of both the front end
and the back end.
A successful website is not only attractive, but also fast, reliable, and easy to use.
On the front end, one of the most important ideas is user experience or UX.
The website should be smooth and enjoyable.
Users should be able to find information quickly without getting lost.
If a website is difficult to use, People will often leave and look for another option.
Another key part of the front end is the user interface.
Interface or UI.
The user interface is the visual design of the website, including buttons, menus, and layout.
A good UI must have clear buttons to go to different parts of the website.
For example, a menu at the top of the page can help users move between sections like Home, About, and Contact.
Designers should also think about the use of negative space.
Negative space is the empty space around text and images.
While it may seem unimportant, it actually makes a big difference.
Good use of negative space helps users focus on important content.
It also makes the website look clean and professional.
Without enough space, a page can feel crowded and hard to read.
Moving to the back end, we find the technical systems that support the website.
One important process is deployment from local development to a public-facing server.
Developers usually build and test a website on their own computer.
First.
This is called local development.
After testing, the website is deployed to an online server so that users can access it.
This step must be done carefully to avoid errors or downtime.
Another key factor on the back end is bandwidth.
Bandwidth refers to how much data can be transferred between the server and the user.
If a website has fast bandwidth, pages load quickly.
This is very important because users do not like waiting.
A slow website can lead to frustration and cause users to leave.
Back-end developers also need to think about performance tools like cache and cookies.
A cache stores data temporarily so that it can be loaded.
faster the next time a user visits the site.
Cookies store small pieces of information about the user, such as login details or preferences.
Good use of cache, cookies, and similar tools can greatly improve the UX.
The core of the back end includes the service.
Server, database, and application programming interface or API.
The server is the computer that hosts the website and sends data.
To users.
The database stores important information such as user accounts or product details.
The API allows different parts of the System to communicate with each other.
For example, an API can connect the website to a payment system.
All of these parts must work well.
Together smoothly.
If the server is slow or the database is not well organized, the website may not function properly.
Similarly, If the API is poorly designed, it can cause errors or security problems.
Even one problem can ruin the entire user experience.
So all parts must work well together.
A good website requires a balance between front end and back end design.
On the front end, developers must focus on the UX with a good UI that is easy to navigate.
Has clear content and uses negative space effectively.
On the back end, they must handle deployment from local development to a public-facing server, ensure fast bandwidth, use cache and
cookies effectively, and Build strong systems with a server, database, and API.
When all of these components are carefully designed, the result is a good website that is Not only useful, but enjoyable to use.
